summary.intent: Recover Phase 37 (Parallel batch upload pipeline) from a previous session where it was added to ROADMAP.md but never committed, then run the full discuss + plan workflow to capture implementation decisions and create executable PLAN.md files.
summary.outcome: Phase 37 context was fully captured with all implementation decisions locked (concurrency pool of 3, new `uploadFiles()` SDK batch method, Web Worker encryption, single publish after full batch drains, TS-only scope), research was conducted, and 2 plans in 2 waves were created and verified with 0 blockers.

repo: Phase 37 was added to ROADMAP.md and its directory created during a prior session but was never committed — it existed only as unstaged local changes when the session resumed.

The current upload pipeline in useDropUpload.ts does N sequential uploadFile() calls, each triggering encrypt → IPFS pin → add FilePointer → publish folder IPNS, resulting in N IPNS publishes for N files.

SDK's uploadFile() is wrapped in withOperation() which serializes all SDK operations, making naive concurrent calls queue rather than run in parallel — Option C (concurrent uploadFile() calls) was ruled out as not viable.

The desktop FUSE layer receives files one-at-a-time via filesystem release() callbacks with no batch context, making a Rust upload_files() batch method useful for API parity but not directly usable by the FUSE layer without a separate write-coalescing layer.

The stale-children race window (another device publishes new children via sync during a long encrypt+pin batch) is a known foot gun in Option A — mitigation is re-read folder metadata just before final publish and merge new children.
Memory spike risk exists if all files encrypt concurrently before any are pinned — solution is pipeline-style processing: encrypt → pin → free ciphertext → next slot, not encrypt-all then pin-all.

code.finding: Sequential file upload loop — iterates files one at a time, calling uploadFile() for each. This is the primary target for parallelization in Phase 37.
uploadFile() does encrypt+pin+publish as one atomic unit inside withOperation() serialization, making it impossible to batch the folder update without a new SDK method.
FUSE release() callback handles one file at a time — no batch context available at this layer, so desktop cannot benefit from upload_files() without a separate write-coalescing layer.
Rust SDK queue implementation — relevant for understanding how desktop upload operations are serialized, confirming desktop uses a different model than the web app.

The worktree was created off main for parallel work context — the plan-phase execution happened in the main working directory while the worktree was made available at ../cipher-box-worktree-parallel.

FUSE write-coalescing for desktop batch publish optimization — separate FUSE architecture change, needs its own phase.
